Review|META 4Q25: Drivers of 1Q26 Accelerating Growth
FUNDAJAN 29, 2026 ∙ PAID
Share
FUNDAA Preview|META 4Q25: 4Q25 Mixed, 1Q26 May Accelerate  
8Mete FUNDAAI · 1月26日Read full story
META Earnings Quick Take
Q4 2025 revenue grew 24% year over year, beating high end guidance by 1.5% and our expectations by 2%.
Q1 2026 revenue guidance shows 26% to 33% growth year over year, well above our expected 22%.
Q4 2025 EPS grew 11% year over year, beating our 6% expectation.
Key Highlights from the Earnings Call
Instagram Reels watch time jumped 30% year over year.
Q4 optimizations boosted Facebook organic feed and video views by 7%.
GEM and sequence learning improvements together drove 3.5% more ad clicks on Facebook and over 1% better conversions on Instagram in Q4.
The new runtime model launched across Instagram Feed, Stories, and Reels lifted conversion rates by 3% in Q4.
We expanded our Andromeda ads engine to run on NVIDIA, AMD, and MTIA chips. Combined with model innovations, this nearly tripled Andromeda’s computing efficiency. In Q1, we’ll expand MTIA to handle core ranking and recommendation training, not just inference.
We reached agreement with the European Commission on changes to our less personalized ads, rolling out this quarter. But we’re watching legal and regulatory challenges in Europe and the US that could seriously impact our business. Youth related scrutiny continues, with several US trials scheduled this year that could result in significant losses.

Despite 2026 CAPEX guidance of \$115 to \$136 billion, we’ll still face capacity constraints.
2026 operating income will exceed 2025 levels.
What Changed?
Where the Beat Came From
The strength comes from accelerating high end guidance by 10%. Zuckerberg mainly credited Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 beats to recommendation algorithm improvements. This eases concerns about CAPEX and OPEX, showing AI investments are paying off.
Where We Missed
We called the Q1 2026 acceleration in our preview. But we overlooked the 3% FX impact and didn’t explicitly model political spending or Apple Store Link-out impact.
What’s Driving Q1 2026 Acceleration?
Q1 2026 high end growth of 34% accelerates 10% from Q4 2025. We think this breaks down as: FX 3% + political spending easy comp 2% + algorithm/product/engagement improvements 3% to 4% + Apple Store link out 1% to 2%.
In our preview, NA Expert 2 specifically noted seeing Q4 2025 engagement gains.
Algorithm Improvements
Beyond Andromeda from the preview, we believe new models went live with significant impact. The key is that better compute cost efficiency lets recommendation algorithms scale larger.
I did see significant progress in META's recommendation algorithm models before my Q3 2025 research, but after the Q3 2025 results and Andromeda fell short of my expectations, I changed my mind and thought the marginal benefits were fading. But clearly they weren't. META proved with newer models that they're still making major improvements.
I deeply regret not maintaining my original thesis.

Apple Store Link Out Impact
Based on our latest checks, non gaming apps started switching to external payments around Christmas, following games. Top games may have 20% to 30% switching rates already. US developers can switch to external payments on Apple, while Japan allows switching on both Apple and Android.
The key change: Apple appealed immediately after the last ruling but hasn’t appealed this time. This makes mobile apps less worried about Apple retaliation.
META gets about 25% of ads from games and mobile apps. Assuming 12% is Apple revenue, with 7% in US and Japan, a 20% increase in ad spending would mean 1.5% revenue lift.
Here’s a simple example: A game company with \$100 in revenue typically spends \$30 on ads and pays \$30 in Apple tax. If Apple tax drops 30%, that saves \$9. If 60% of those savings go to ads, ad spending rises 20%.
Model Update
We now estimate FY2026 revenue growth of 27% year over year, OPEX \$162B, CAPEX \$128B, EPS \$32.26 up 9% year over year.
For FY2027: revenue growth 20% year over year, OPEX \$208B, CAPEX \$148B, EPS \$34.13 up 6% year over year.
